overview: MOVe Logistics Group (formerly TIL Logistics Group, rebranded ~2022; listed on the NZX Main Board and secondary-listed on the ASX since a December 2017 reverse listing with Bethunes Investments) is one of New Zealand's largest domestic freight and logistics operators, built from a roll-up of over 150 years' worth of regional trucking and logistics businesses. It operates a nationwide network of ~39 branches, warehouses, depots and crossdocks with 500+ trucks and ~96,000 m² of warehouse space, servicing customers across general freight, bulk-liquid/fuel tankers, warehousing/3PL, specialist heavy haulage, and international freight forwarding/shipping agency (including a trans-Tasman Oceans shipping service). The company is currently ~18 months into a two-year 'Accelerate' cost-out and network-rightsizing turnaround (FY25-FY26) following a severe earnings collapse in FY2023-FY2024, after which management pivots to a four-year 'New Horizons' roadmap targeting FY28.

business_model.summary: MOVe earns revenue from moving and storing freight for New Zealand businesses across five reporting segments: Freight & Fuel (general nationwide trucking plus bulk fuel tanker delivery – the largest segment at roughly two-thirds of group revenue), Warehousing (contracted 3PL/warehousing and supply-chain capability), Specialist (oversized/heavy haulage via Tranzcarr Heavy Haulage and Machinery Movers), International (freight forwarding, shipping agency, and the Oceans trans-Tasman shipping service), and Corporate. Revenue is largely transactional/contract-based (freight rates, warehousing fees, tanker delivery contracts) rather than subscription-style recurring revenue, though many relationships are multi-year strategic partnerships (e.g., 17-year fuel distribution relationship with Z Energy covering 500+ retail sites). The customer base is B2B across retail, FMCG, fuel/energy, construction, infrastructure, aquaculture and primary produce; ~70% of the top 20 clients are retail-sector exposed. Only one customer contributes more than 10% of group revenue (in Freight & Fuel). FY25 sales revenue was $286.3m (down 2.6% YoY from $293.9m); H1-2026 (six months to Dec-2025) revenue was $141.4m (down ~5% YoY) as the company continues to prioritise margin over volume amid a weak New Zealand economy.

revenue_streams.name: Freight & Fuel (general freight + bulk liquid/tanker delivery)

business_model.customer_type: B2B – large national retail/FMCG/fuel/energy accounts down to regional SME shippers; long-term contracted partnerships alongside spot/tender freight work
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily New Zealand domestic (nationwide network across North and South Islands); International segment adds Australia (TNL Australia Pty Ltd, trans-Tasman Oceans shipping) and a Singapore entity (MOVe Oceans Singapore) for shipping/chartering operations

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier national player in a moderately concentrated, roughly NZ$10bn+ New Zealand freight and logistics market; a distant challenger to market leader Mainfreight (NZ$3.5bn+ global revenue) and specialist courier/healthcare logistics player Freightways, but retains meaningful scale and national reach built from decades of regional trucking consolidation

moat_factors.description: 39 branches/depots/crossdocks nationwide give reach that smaller regional operators lack, and support integrated end-to-end freight, warehousing and specialist offerings
17-year Z Energy fuel distribution relationship (2bn+ litres/year, 99.7% delivery success) and other long-standing contracted customers create switching costs and recurring volume

Tranzcarr Heavy Haulage/Machinery Movers is one of the largest precast-concrete/oversized-freight carriers in NZ with proprietary heavy-lift gantry systems – a niche few competitors can service, generating the group's best segment margins
150+ year operating heritage across legacy regional brands rolled into MOVe, but the brand has been damaged by the FY23-25 financial distress, cost-cutting and leadership turnover
Materially smaller and less capitalised than Mainfreight; lacks Mainfreight's owned-property/vertically integrated global network and Freightways' parcel-network density, limiting pricing power

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus Mainfreight in trans-Tasman and warehousing, limiting bargaining power on rates and driving margin compression under 'irrational' competitor pricing
Warehousing division structurally challenged by excess market capacity, customers reverting to just-in-time inventory models, and storage pricing below pre-COVID levels
High customer concentration risk in a retail/FMCG-heavy book (~70% of top-20 clients) makes revenue highly sensitive to NZ consumer spending cycles

Balance sheet still working through a going-concern-flagged working-capital deficit and near-term debt refinancing, constraining capital available for growth investment versus better-capitalised peers
Small free float / thin analyst coverage (no sell-side analyst questions on the H1-2026 earnings call) limits liquidity and market scrutiny

growth_drivers: Completion of the 'Accelerate' transformation programme (FY25-FY26): ~$27m of annualised cost-out delivered in FY25, network rightsizing (new Dunedin freight branch, exit of two underutilised warehouse sites), and a shift from 'reset' to 'value creation' from FY26

Freight & Fuel margin recovery: division NEBT loss improved ~90% YoY in FY25 and turned NEBT-positive by 4Q25/H1-2026, driven by route optimisation, fleet rationalisation (shift to leased trucks) and pricing discipline
Warehousing reset under new leadership (GM appointed Feb 2025): new customer wins commencing 1H26, site consolidation expected to lift financial performance in FY26

International/Oceans trans-Tasman shipping pilot (time-charter of the larger, faster 'Brio Faith' vessel) delivered a second consecutive profitable half in H1-2026, with capacity available to add smaller customers
Specialist division healthy multi-year pipeline in renewable energy/power generation and Pacific infrastructure projects, with roading project upside expected from FY27

Structural tailwind from the retirement of the only rail-enabled Cook Strait ferry (until new vessels arrive ~2029), positioning MOVe's South Island logistics hubs to capture freight rerouted around reduced ferry rail capacity

Four-year 'New Horizons' roadmap (Reset FY25-26 → Step Up FY26-27 → Stand Out FY28) targeting market-share gains as the NZ economy recovers and MOVe's lower cost base becomes a relative advantage over less-disciplined competitors
New BNZ invoice-financing facility (effective Nov 2026) replacing the more expensive PIFNZ facility, expected to reduce finance costs and improve working-capital efficiency

business.risk: Revenue concentration in retail/FMCG cyclical demand
business.description: ~70% of top-20 clients are retail-sector exposed; NZ consumer recession has directly compressed freight volumes across FY24-26

Excess market warehouse capacity, customers reverting to just-in-time models, and intense/irrational competitor pricing have driven storage rates below pre-COVID levels; division remains the weakest performer despite a reset
One customer contributes >10% of group revenue within Freight & Fuel; loss or renegotiation of key contracts (e.g., Z Energy) would be material

Turnaround relies on sustained cost discipline and network optimisation continuing to convert into earnings; the FY24 change programme itself replaced an earlier failed 'Project Blueprint' initiative, showing prior execution missteps

financial.description: As at 31-Dec-2025 the group had a working capital deficit of $39.2m (of which $28.1m is current lease liability) and loans/borrowings due for refinancing within 12 months; directors concluded no material uncertainty only after securing amended ANZ covenants and a new BNZ facility post period-end

financial.risk: Thin equity base / high leverage relative to size
financial.description: Total equity of only $10.6m against total liabilities of $209.1m at Dec-2025 (accumulated losses of $76.8m); equity attributable to owners is just $7.2m, leaving very little buffer against further shocks
ANZ facility covenants (fixed charge cover ratio, guarantor asset/EBITDA coverage, capex caps) were renegotiated twice in the past year; further underperformance could trigger fresh covenant breaches

Right-of-use assets ($132.0m) and lease liabilities ($147.0m combined current+non-current) dwarf bank borrowings ($21.4m), meaning reported EBITDA/cashflow must be read alongside substantial lease-related cash outflows (~$14.9m lease principal repaid in H1-2026 alone)

regulatory.description: NZ climate-reporting regime (second year of mandatory climate disclosures in FY25) and potential future heavy-vehicle emissions standards could raise fleet transition costs
Government policy on road-user charges, driver licensing and heavy-vehicle regulation affects operating costs across the trucking industry broadly

macro.description: Management explicitly cites 'recessionary economy,' reduced customer demand/volumes and intensifying competition as the primary drag on FY24-26 results; timing of economic recovery remains uncertain

Company carries secured bank borrowings, lease finance costs (~$3.8m in H1-2026) and receivables-funding facilities; higher-for-longer NZ rates increase finance costs and refinancing risk given the near-term facility maturities

Transport costs (fuel, driver wages) are the largest expense line (~$57.6m of $139.1m total expenses in H1-2026); diesel price swings and wage inflation directly compress margins if not passed through

Specialist division has been hit by a sharp contraction in construction (precast concrete volumes dropped below 20% of typical levels in FY25); recovery depends on infrastructure and roading project timing, some of which management does not expect to ramp until FY27

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The New Zealand freight and logistics market is estimated by management at NZ$10bn+ and is forecast to grow moderately over 2026-2031, but near-term conditions remain soft with a slow, uneven consumer-led recovery; the sector faces intensifying competition and excess warehousing capacity industry-wide
macro_factors.cyclicality: High – freight volumes closely track NZ consumer spending, retail activity, construction/infrastructure investment and general economic conditions; MOVe's FY23-25 results directly mirror the NZ recession
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high given near-term debt refinancing needs, working-capital funding facilities (invoice financing) and heavy lease liabilities carrying imputed finance costs

recent_developments.event: FY26 (year ended 30 June 2026) audited results scheduled for release 25 August 2026 with a live investor briefing; per a 24-July-2026 trading update the company confirmed it achieved its target of positive full-year normalised EBT for FY26, with revenue growing with 'increasing momentum,' improved gross margin, reduced net debt, restored positive free cashflow, and three of four divisions (Freight & Fuel, Specialist, International) profitable while Warehousing remains the outlier

H1-2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) results: revenue $141.4m (down ~5% YoY), Normalised EBT improved 98% YoY to ~$(0.1)-$(0.2)m, net loss after tax narrowed to $(0.5)m from $(8.6)m, operating cashflow up to $17.0m (+$8.1m YoY), net debt reduced. International division delivered a second consecutive profitable half

Group reached agreement with ANZ to vary financial covenants (fixed charge cover ratio, guarantor coverage, capex limits) and quarterly repayment terms, and signed a committed new invoice-funding facility with BNZ (effective Nov-2026, expiring 31-Aug-2027) to replace the existing PIFNZ receivables-funding facility, explicitly to address the going-concern working-capital deficit

FY25 results: sales revenue $286.3m (down 2.6%), NEBT improved 61% to $(10.0)m, net loss after tax narrowed by $32.5m to $(15.6)m, operating cashflow up 35% to $25.3m, positive adjusted net operating cashflow of $0.3m achieved (vs. -$5.9m in FY24); four consecutive quarters of improving NEBT with the strongest quarterly NEBT in two years in 4Q25; ~$27m of annualised operating cost reductions delivered under the 'Accelerate' programme

Paul Millward (former CEO of 2 Cheap Cars/2CC.NZ, which he led through its own NZX turnaround) confirmed as permanent CEO after joining as interim CEO in September 2024; extended ANZ bank facility term to August 2026 (subsequently further extended to Aug 2027)

Board and leadership overhaul: long-standing directors Lorraine Witten, Mark Newman and Grant Devonport stepped down; Julia Raue (ex-Air NZ CIO, ex-Warehouse Group/Z Energy director) appointed Chair (June 2024); new general managers appointed across Freight & Fuel, Warehousing and People & Culture during FY25

Divested the older Oceans trans-Tasman shipping vessel and moved to a time-charter model with the larger, faster 'Brio Faith,' and continued sale of surplus/aging fleet assets as part of network rightsizing

NAOS Asset Management increased its substantial shareholding to 17.66% (from 16.59%); a separate substantial holder (Christopher Dunphy) reduced from 6.386% to 1.946% after a lapsed call option arrangement – no takeover offer or scheme of arrangement identified as at Aug-2026

guidance.as_of: H1-2026 results (26 Feb 2026) and 24 Jul 2026 pre-FY26-results trading update

items.notes: Management guided at FY25 results (Aug-2025) that the company remained 'on track to return to positive normalised EBT in FY26'; reaffirmed on the H1-2026 call (Feb-2026); confirmed as achieved in the 24-Jul-2026 trading update ahead of the 25-Aug-2026 audited FY26 results release. FY25 NEBT was $(10.0)m and H1-2026 NEBT was roughly break-even, implying the full FY26 NEBT swing depended on H2-2026
24-Jul-2026 update cites 'positive free cashflow was restored' for FY26, alongside reduced net debt and borrowings, following FY25's positive adjusted net operating cashflow of only $0.3m

items.target: ~$27m annualised opex reduction (delivered FY25); full benefits realised in FY26
items.notes: Comprising ~$15m labour savings and ~$12m other cost-out/efficiency; FY25 letter states 'the full benefits of the cost out programme [are] to be realised in the current year' (FY26)

items.target: Restricted to 110% of approved FY26 budget
items.notes: Covenant condition agreed with ANZ as part of the Feb-2026 facility amendment; reflects continued capital discipline while selectively renewing fleet

items.target: Warehousing to deliver 'better financial outcomes' in FY26 from site consolidation and new customer contracts commencing 1H26
items.notes: Per the 24-Jul-2026 update, Warehousing remained the one underperforming division even as the other three turned profitable, so this remains a work-in-progress rather than a delivered target

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Paul Millward: FY26 'represents an important milestone, as the company delivered on its financial target and strengthened the business to be leaner and more capable,' citing 'increased revenue and positive earnings (NEBT) amidst an inconsistent economy and intense competition.' On the H1-2026 call he noted the group is transitioning from 'reset' to growth initiatives, with 'structural benefits...now being delivered,' while flagging persistent economic uncertainty, irrational short-term pricing behaviour from Warehousing competitors, and dependence on gradual NZ consumer/economic recovery through 2026. No sell-side analyst questions were raised on the H1-2026 call.

bull_case: Turnaround is tracking on plan: four consecutive quarters of improving NEBT through FY25, a 98% YoY NEBT improvement in H1-2026, and confirmation (Jul-2026) that the company hit its target of positive full-year normalised EBT for FY26 – the clearest inflection signal yet after two years of heavy losses
~$27m of annualised structural cost-out is now largely embedded, so incremental revenue recovery as the NZ economy improves should convert at materially higher operating leverage than in FY23-24

Three of four divisions (Freight & Fuel, Specialist, International) are now consistently profitable, with the Oceans trans-Tasman shipping pilot delivering two consecutive profitable halves and a healthy multi-year Specialist project pipeline in energy/infrastructure

Refinancing risk is being actively de-risked: amended, less onerous ANZ covenants and a new lower-cost BNZ invoice-finance facility (from Nov-2026) reduce near-term liquidity/going-concern pressure that weighed on the stock through FY24-25

Experienced turnaround CEO (Paul Millward, who led 2 Cheap Cars/2CC.NZ through a comparable NZX turnaround) plus a refreshed, smaller board gives some confidence in execution discipline for the remaining 'Step Up' and 'Stand Out' phases of the four-year roadmap
bear_case: Balance sheet remains fragile: $10.6m total equity (just $7.2m attributable to owners) against $209m of liabilities and a $39.2m working-capital deficit at Dec-2025, with debt/lease facilities up for renewal within 12 months – any relapse in trading would quickly reopen going-concern questions

Warehousing division remains structurally impaired by industry-wide excess capacity and 'irrational' competitor pricing, with no clear timeline to profitability despite two years of reset efforts, and it is a meaningful (~15% of revenue) drag on group earnings

Revenue is still shrinking (down 2.6% in FY25, down ~5% in H1-2026) – the improvement story so far has been entirely cost-out and margin-driven, not demand-driven, leaving execution highly dependent on an uncertain and so-far-elusive NZ economic recovery

Company is sub-scale versus Mainfreight and Freightways, limiting pricing power, network density and ability to invest in automation/technology that larger, better-capitalised competitors can fund, risking share loss once demand does return

Thin free float, no sell-side coverage, and history of strategy resets (the FY24 'Accelerate' plan itself replaced a failed earlier 'Project Blueprint' initiative) mean investors have limited independent scrutiny of whether the current roadmap will be executed better than prior turnaround attempts
